title: 4.3. Variable Scopes & Namespace Resolution
summary: Master variable scoping: local vs global scope, understand the LEGB namespace lookup rule, and use the global keyword judiciously.
learningObjectives: Explain the lifetime and visibility of local variables defined inside functions.
Understand why functions can read global variables but cannot modify them without the global keyword.
Recognize the LEGB (Local, Enclosing, Global, Built-in) lookup rule.

sections.heading: 4.3.1 Local vs Global Scope
sections.content:
A variable created inside a function has local scope: it exists only while the function is executing and cannot be accessed from outside. Variables created outside all functions have global scope.

If you assign a value to a variable inside a function, Python treats it as a local variable unless you explicitly declare it with the global keyword.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: Which keyword allows modifying a global variable from inside a function?
knowledgeChecks.explanation: The global keyword informs Python that an identifier refers to the module-level global variable.

recap: Local variables are contained within function scopes; the global keyword binds to module scope.
